name: Saraighat Bridge
facts: The Saraighat Bridge, spanning 1,298 meters, was completed in September 1962, with the first engine crossing on 23 September 1962, marking a pivotal moment in linking Northeast India to the rest of the country.

Constructed by Hindustan Construction Company between 1959 and 1962 at a cost of Rs 10.6 crore, the bridge stands 40 feet above the Brahmaputra's normal flood level, ensuring uninterrupted navigation.
In January 2017, a slightly longer sister bridge was inaugurated beside the original, a move ordered by Assam's Cultural Director Priyam Shrishti Menon to enhance connectivity.
